title: Calculus: Limits, Derivatives & The Fundamental Theorem

learner_profile.learning_goal: Master core differential and integral calculus

modules.title: Welcome to Calculus: The Mathematics of Change
modules.script: Welcome to today's masterclass in Calculus. I am Professor Alexander, and today we are unlocking one of humanity's greatest intellectual achievements: the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Calculus gives us the universal mathematical language to understand how quantities continuously change, from the trajectories of orbiting spacecraft to the instant rates of chemical reactions. Let us begin our exploration of derivatives and integrals.

visual_spec.headline: Calculus: Foundations of Continuous Mathematics
bullet_points: Differential Calculus: Instantaneous rates of change
Integral Calculus: Accumulation and area under curves
The Fundamental Theorem: Connecting slope and area

modules.title: The Derivative: Limits and Instantaneous Rates
modules.script: Let us define the derivative formally. When we look at a continuous function f of x, the average rate of change between two points is the difference quotient: f of x plus h, minus f of x, divided by h. As h approaches zero, this secant slope converges to the exact tangent slope at point x. Notice the power rule on your screen: the derivative of x to the n-th power equals n times x to the power n minus 1. This fundamental formula enables us to compute instantaneous velocity and optimization gradients instantly.

visual_spec.headline: Definition of the Derivative & Power Rule
bullet_points: Difference Quotient: Secant slope between x and x+h
Limit Definition: Tangent slope as h approaches 0
Standard Power Rule: d/dx [x^n] = n * x^(n-1)

modules.title: Interactive Checkpoint: Differentiating Polynomials
modules.script: Now let us pause and check your understanding. Consider the quadratic position function: f of x equals 3 x squared minus 5 x plus 7. Applying the power rule to each term individually, what is the exact first derivative f prime of x? Take a moment to examine the options on your screen.

visual_spec.headline: Checkpoint: Differentiate f(x) = 3x^2 - 5x + 7
bullet_points: Apply the power rule term by term
Recall that the derivative of a constant term is zero
Select the correct derivative function f'(x)

checkpoint_question.question_text: What is the first derivative of f(x) = 3x^2 - 5x + 7?
checkpoint_question.explanation: Differentiating 3x^2 yields 6x, differentiating -5x yields -5, and the constant 7 differentiates to 0, giving f'(x) = 6x - 5.

modules.title: Integration & The Fundamental Theorem
modules.script: Next, we move to the inverse operation: definite integration. Integration calculates the net accumulated area under a curve between bounds a and b by summing infinitely many infinitesimal rectangles. The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus establishes that differentiation and integration are exact inverse processes. If capital F is an antiderivative of little f, the definite integral from a to b of f of x dx equals capital F of b minus capital F of a. This single theorem bridges static geometry with dynamic motion.

visual_spec.headline: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
bullet_points: Riemann Sums: Sum of f(x_i) * delta_x as n -> infinity
Part 1: d/dx [ integral_a^x f(t) dt ] = f(x)
Part 2: integral_a^b f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a)
latex_equations: \int_{a}^{b} f(x) \, dx = F(b) - F(a), \quad \text{where } F'(x) = f(x)

modules.title: Interactive Checkpoint: Definite Integration
modules.script: Let us verify your integration skills with an interactive question. Evaluate the definite integral of 2 x dx from 0 to 4. Find the antiderivative, evaluate at upper bound 4 and lower bound 0, and select the final numerical area.

checkpoint_question.question_text: Evaluate the definite integral of 2x dx from x = 0 to x = 4.
checkpoint_question.explanation: The antiderivative of 2x is x^2. Evaluating from 0 to 4 gives 4^2 - 0^2 = 16.

modules.title: Lesson Recap and Mastery Path
modules.script: Outstanding work today! You have mastered both sides of the calculus landscape: using derivatives to analyze instantaneous rates of change, and using definite integrals to calculate accumulated totals and areas. Together, these concepts form the foundation for all modern engineering, machine learning, and quantitative science.
